title: Review of petitions for rulemaking: APA §§ 553(e) and 555(e)
shortTitle: Review of petitions for rulemaking: APA §§ 553(e) and 555(e)
summary: A petition asks an agency to issue, amend, or repeal a rule; denial can supply a reviewable decision whose reasons must fit the governing statute.
notes:
Section 553(e) permits interested persons to petition for issuance, amendment, or repeal of a rule. Section 555(e) generally requires a brief statement of grounds when an agency denies a covered request. Massachusetts v. EPA treats the denial in its statutory setting as reviewable, while distinguishing enforcement refusal and preserving substantial administrative discretion.

American Horse Protection v. Lyng illustrates a developed record: the agency had studied a tentative rule, held meetings, prepared amendments, and acknowledged an apparent inconsistency with later research before declining to proceed. The court remanded for explanation. Later note cases show the limits: absence of applicable standards can still defeat review; where review occurs it may be very deferential, though a failure to address a central safety matter on an empty record can warrant intervention.

The editors pose a statutory question rather than concealing it: a petition can seek to initiate a proceeding rather than arise within one, and the text of § 555(e) refers to requests connected with agency proceedings. They weigh this concern against the broad APA definition of action, including denials and failures to act. A reason-giving obligation does not automatically settle standing, finality, reviewability, or entitlement to a particular substantive rule.
